I have had this idea to spread some wild flower seeds along roadways. But if I just throw seeds out of my vehicle while driving they will most likely just end up on the road. So I need something I can throw further. Across the lane and across the highway shoulder, maybe even over the ditch. What could I embed a bunch of seeds in to give them a good chance of growing? Something that holds it's shape enough for me to throw it.

My best attempt at a "seed bomb" would probably be like making cookie dough, take some potting soil and mash seeds into it like you're making meatloaf. Add clay until you get something that won't fall apart, then stick it in the fridge to keep the seeds from germinating too soon.

Keep in mind that what /u/VoatAntacid said is pretty accurate, areas near roads are mowed regularly and the established grass will be taking up any available growing space for your flowers! Your most likely outcome would be a few flowers that quickly get drowned out by tall grass and eventually mowed away.

That said, there are some hardier species you could try than wildflowers. Why not some ground cover varieties? There are several that do well in full sun and can even outcompete grasses for space. Problem is, that kind of plant is likely to be thought of as a weed or invasive species. Creeping Charlie is exactly the kind of hardy ground cover I'm discussing, and we hate that stuff around here. Only redeeming quality it has is that you can eat it.
